name: Sale, VAT 16 %
description: A taxable supply made in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines by a registered person, standard-rated
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 445, s. 8(1)-(3)(d) — VAT is levied on a taxable supply and a taxable import; in any other case than zero-rating, accommodation and tourist services the standard rate applies; s. 8(4) — the VAT on a supply is the liability of the supplier. Rate: the revised edition of the Act in the Inland Revenue Department's legislation page (issue 1/2009) states 15 percent (s. 8(3)(d)) and 10 percent for accommodation (s. 8(3)(b)); the Department's page "Taxes" and its FAQ give the current rates as 16 percent standard and 11 percent for accommodation. The amending instrument was not found; the 1 May 2017 date comes from the Budget Address of 2017 as reported by the press. The base posts to box 1 net of the tax, the tax to box 7 (box numbers are this pack's, see tax_report.json).

name: Retail sale, VAT 16 %, the price includes the tax
description: A standard-rated sale whose price already holds the VAT
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 445, s. 8(3)(d) at the standard rate (16 percent, see VC-S-16 for the source of the rate), applied to a price that already holds the tax — what price_include does: 116.00 holds 100.00 and 16.00. The Act's own definition of the value of a supply whose price includes the tax was not located. Same boxes as VC-S-16.

name: Sale of accommodation or tourist services, VAT 11 %
description: Holiday or hotel accommodation (stays of fewer than forty-five days) and the tourist services of s. 8(3)(b), at the reduced rate
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 445, s. 8(3)(b) — a reduced rate for holiday or hotel accommodation, accommodation in a caravan, houseboat, camping site, boat or marina berth for a continuous period of less than forty-five days, and for diving, marine or land tour services and other services ordinarily provided to tourists that the Minister prescribes by order. The 2009 edition says 10 percent; the Department's pages give the current accommodation rate as 11 percent ("Accommodation (Rooms) — 11%"). No official text read for this pack states the rate of the tourist services after 2017: the press report of the 2017 Budget Address raises accommodation and other tourism-related activities from 10 to 11 percent, and the pack carries 11 percent for both until a reviewer checks the order. Stays beyond forty-five days under a landlord and tenant agreement are exempt (Fourth Schedule, items 7 and 8) and go to VC-S-EX. Base to box 2, tax to box 8.

name: Sale of diving, tour or other tourist services, VAT 11 %
description: Diving, marine or land tour services and other services ordinarily provided to tourists, at the reduced rate
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 445, s. 8(3)(b)(iii) (inserted by S.R.O. 41 of 2007, amended by Act No. 1 of 2008) — diving services, marine or land tour services and any other service ordinarily provided to tourists or visitors that the Minister prescribes by order; 10 percent in the 2009 edition, carried at 11 percent with the accommodation rate (see VC-S-11). The orders listing the prescribed services were not read: the pack does not decide which services qualify, and a restaurant's food and drink is not a tourist service in this pack. Base to box 3, tax to box 9.

name: Zero-rated supply (export)
description: An export of goods or a service consumed outside Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, zero-rated
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 445, s. 8(3)(a) — zero per cent for a zero-rated supply; First Schedule (goods exported or located outside the country, supplies to duty-free vendors) and Second Schedule (services connected with exported goods, services consumed outside the country, telecommunications, international financial services). The zero-rated supply stays on the return. valid_from is 1 May 2007, the implementation date given by the Department's FAQ.

name: Zero-rated supply in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
description: A domestic supply of the Third Schedule at zero per cent (basic foods, residential electricity and water, fuel, exercise books, newspapers, computers, solar equipment, hygiene items)
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 445, Third Schedule (zero-rated supplies and imports: other) — items 1 to 14: listed foods (white rice, cane sugar, milk, flour, cooking oil, salt and others), the first 200 kWh a month of residential electricity, gasoline, kerosene, diesel and LPG, exercise books, newspapers, computers, residential water, the service charge within the limits of item 11, hygiene goods, solar water heaters and solar panels. The list of food items grew after the 2009 edition: the Cabinet decision of 29 October 2025 zero-rated nine more items (other chicken parts, processed cheddar cheese, canned tuna and sardines, chicken sausages, cereals, lentils, health drinks, adult diapers) from 3 November 2025. The pack does not reproduce the list; whether a supply is on it is the user's to check against the Act and the Regulations. valid_from is 1 May 2007, the implementation date.

name: Exempt supply
description: A supply of the Fourth Schedule (financial services, insurance, sale of real property, residential rent, stays of more than forty-five days, passenger transport), outside the tax
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 445, Fourth Schedule (exempt supplies), paragraph 1, items 2 to 10: financial services and insurance, supplies of goods used solely to make exempt supplies, international transport, the sale of real property, residential leases, long stays under a landlord and tenant agreement, supplies by a condominium body corporate to a member and the transport of passengers within the country. Reported on the return for information; the input tax of what is acquired to make them is not recoverable. The remaining items (health, education and the like) were not read in full and are not listed. valid_from is 1 May 2007.

name: Purchase, VAT 16 %
description: A purchase from a registered person, standard-rated, with a VAT invoice
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 445, s. 29 — input tax credits for a taxable person on what is acquired for a taxable activity, on the strength of a VAT invoice (s. 32); rate as VC-S-16. The pack treats all the tax on a business purchase as recoverable; the denials of s. 28 (passenger vehicles, entertainment) are the user's. Base to box 12, tax to box 14.

name: Purchase of accommodation or tourist services, VAT 11 %
description: Accommodation or tourist services bought for the business at the reduced rate
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 445, s. 29 and s. 8(3)(b) — the input tax on accommodation or tourist services acquired for the taxable activity, at 11 percent (see VC-S-11 for the rate). Base to box 12, tax to box 14.

name: Import of goods, VAT 16 %
description: Goods imported: the VAT paid to the Comptroller of Customs
legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 445, s. 8(1)(b) and (2) — VAT is levied on a taxable import, the rate applied to its value; s. 29 for the credit; rate as VC-S-16. The pack applies 16 percent to the invoice value; the value for VAT of an import (with duty and freight) is the customs entry's. Base to box 11, tax to box 13.

name: Purchase without VAT
description: A purchase of a zero-rated or exempt supply, or from a person who charges no VAT: no input tax to claim
legal_reference: A purchase of a zero-rated or exempt supply, or from a person who charges no VAT, carries no input tax to claim (Value Added Tax Act, Cap. 445, s. 29 allows the credit for tax actually charged on a VAT invoice). Base to box 12.
